q: Find the area of quadrilateral formed by joining points (4, 2), (8, 2), (8, 14) and (4, 10).
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Area of }}\Delta ABC \\ & = \frac{1}{2}\left[ {{x_1}\left( {{y_2} - {y_3}} \right) + {x_2}\left( {{y_3} - {y_1}} \right) + {x_3}\left( {{y_1} - {y_2}} \right)} \right] \\ & = \frac{1}{2}\left[ {4\left( {2 - 14} \right) + 8\left( {14 - 2} \right) + 8\left( {2 - 2} \right)} \right] \\ & = \frac{1}{2}\left[ {4 \times \left( { - 12} \right) + 8\left( {12} \right) + 8\left( 0 \right)} \right] \\ & = \frac{1}{2}\left[ { - 48 + 96} \right] \\ & = \frac{1}{2} \times 48 \\ & = 24{\text{ sq}}{\text{. units}} \\ & {\text{Area of }}\Delta ACD \\ & = \frac{1}{2}\left[ {{x_1}\left( {{y_2} - {y_3}} \right) + {x_2}\left( {{y_3} - {y_1}} \right) + {x_3}\left( {{y_1} - {y_2}} \right)} \right] \\ & = \frac{1}{2}\left[ {4\left( {14 - 10} \right) + 8\left( {10 - 2} \right) + 4\left( {2 - 14} \right)} \right] \\ & = \frac{1}{2}\left[ {4 \times 4 + 8 \times 8 + 4 \times \left( { - 12} \right)} \right] \\ & = \frac{1}{2}\left[ {16 + 64 - 48} \right] \\ & = \frac{1}{2} \times 32 \\ & = 16{\text{ sq}}{\text{. units}} \\ & {\text{Hence Area of Quadrilateral }}ABCD \\ & = {\text{Area of }}\left( {\Delta ABC + \Delta ACD} \right) \\ & = 24 + 16 \\ & = 40{\text{ sq}}{\text{. units}} \end{aligned}$$

q: For triangle ABC, find equation of median AD if co-ordinates of points A, B and C are (2, -4), (3, 0) and (5, -2) respectively?
s: Co-ordinates of mid point (D) which lies on the line BC = $$\left( {\frac{{3 + 5}}{2},\,\frac{{0 - 2}}{2}} \right) = \left( {4,\, - 1} \right)$$ Now, Co-ordinates of line AD = A(2, -4), D(4, -1) ∴ Equation of the line which passes through the two point (x 1 , y 1 ), & (x 2 , y 2 ) ⇒ y - y 1 = m(x - x 1 ) ∴ required equation of the line = y + 4 = m(x - 2) $$\begin{aligned} & \left[ {\because m = \frac{{{y_2} - {y_1}}}{{{x_2} - {x_1}}}} \right] \\ & \therefore m = \frac{{ - 1 + 4}}{{4 - 2}} = \frac{3}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow y + 4 = \frac{3}{2}\left[ {x - 2} \right] \\ & \Rightarrow 2y + 8 = 3x - 6 \\ & \Rightarrow 3x - 2y = 14 \end{aligned}$$

q: What is the equation of the line whose y-intercept is $$- \frac{3}{4}$$ and making an angle of 45° with the positive x-axis?

q: Find k, if the line 4x - y = 1 is perpendicular to the line 5x - ky = 2?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Given,}} \\ & 4x - y = 1 \\ & \therefore y = 4x - 1 \\ & 5x - ky = 2 \\ & \therefore y = \frac{{5x}}{k} - \frac{2}{k} \\ & y = {m_1}x + C \\ & {m_1} = \frac{5}{k} \end{aligned}$$ If the lines are ⊥ then the product of their slope is -1 \[\begin{array}{l} {m_1} \times {m_2} = - 1\\ 4 \times \frac{5}{k} = - 1\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\left\{ \begin{array}{l} {m_1} = 4\\ {m_2} = \frac{5}{k} \end{array} \right.\\ \therefore k = - 20 \end{array}\]

q: The line passing through (-2, 5) and (6, b) is perpendicular to the line 20x + 5y = 3. Find b?
s: Equation of given line $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 20x + 5y = 3 \\ & \Rightarrow 5y = 3 - 20x \\ & \Rightarrow y = - 4x + \frac{3}{5} \end{aligned}$$ Slope of line, m 1 = -4 If two are lines are ⊥ then the product of their slope = -1 $$\begin{aligned} & {m_1} \times {m_2} = - 1 \\ & - 4 \times {m_2} = - 1 \\ & {m_2} = \frac{1}{4} \end{aligned}$$ Lines passing through the points (-2, 5) and (6, b) Therefore, $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Slope}} = \frac{{{y_2} - {y_1}}}{{{x_2} - {x_1}}} = \frac{{b - 5}}{{6 + 2}} = \frac{{b - 5}}{8} \\ & {\text{According to the question,}} \\ & \frac{{b - 5}}{8} = \frac{1}{4} \\ & b - 5 = 2 \\ & \therefore b = 7 \end{aligned}$$

q: Find k, if the line 2x - 3y = 11 is perpendicular to the line 3x + ky = -4?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & 2x - 3y = 11 \\ & 3y = 2x - 11 \\ & y = \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{{11}}{3} \\ & \left( {y = mx + c,{\text{ where }}m{\text{ is slope}}} \right) \\ & {\text{Slope}} = {m_1} = \frac{2}{3} \\ & 3x + ky = - 4 \\ & ky = - 3x - 4 \\ & y = - \frac{3}{k}x - \frac{4}{k} \\ & {m_2} = - \frac{3}{k} \end{aligned}$$ Relation between slope of perpendicular lines $$\begin{aligned} & {m_1}{m_2} = - 1 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {\frac{2}{3}} \right) \times \left( { - \frac{3}{k}} \right) = 1 \\ & \Rightarrow k = 2 \end{aligned}$$

q: The graph of 3x + 4y - 24 = 0 forms a triangle OAB with the co-ordinate axes, where O is the origin. Also the graph of x + y + 4 = 0 forms a triangle OCD with the coordinate axes. Then the area of ∆OCD is equal to:

q: The distance between the points (4, 8) and (k, -4) is 13. What is the value of k?

q: The slope of the line passing through the points (2, -1) and (x, 5) is -1. Find x?

q: The points A(3, -2), B(1, 4) and C(-2, x) are collinear. What is the value of x?

q: What will be the equation of the perpendicular bisector of segment joining the points (5, -3) and (0, 2)?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{O is mid point of AB}} \\ & x = \frac{{5 + 0}}{2} = \frac{5}{2} \\ & y = \frac{{ - 3 + 2}}{2} = \frac{{ - 1}}{2} \\ & {\text{Slope of AB }}\left( {{m_1}} \right) \\ & = \frac{{{y_2} - {y_1}}}{{{x_2} - {x_1}}} \\ & = \frac{{2 - \left( { - 3} \right)}}{{0 - 5}} \\ & = \frac{5}{{ - 5}} \\ & = - 1 \end{aligned}$$ Slope of (m 2 ) CD = 1 [lines are perpendicular to each other] m 1 × m 2 = -1 Equation of line $$\begin{aligned} & \left( {y + \frac{1}{2}} \right) = 1\left( {x - \frac{5}{2}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow 2\left( {x - y} \right) = 6 \\ & \Rightarrow x - y = 3 \end{aligned}$$

q: The graph of the linear equation 3x + 4y = 24 is a straight line intersecting x-axis and y-axis at the points A and B respectively. P(2, 0) and Q$$\left( {0,\,\frac{3}{2}} \right)$$ are two points on the sides OA and OB respectively of ∆OAB, where O is the origin of the co-ordinate system. Given that AB = 10 cm, then PQ = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{By distance formula, }} \\ & {\text{PQ}} = \sqrt {{{\left( {0 - 2} \right)}^2} + {{\left( {\frac{3}{2} - 0} \right)}^2}} \\ & = \sqrt {4 + \frac{9}{4}} \\ & = \frac{{\sqrt {25} }}{2} \\ & = \frac{5}{2} \\ & = 2.5{\text{ cm}} \end{aligned}$$

q: What is the equation of a line having slope $$- \frac{1}{3}$$ and y-intercept equal to 6?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \left( {y - {y_1}} \right) = \left( {\frac{{{y_2} - {y_1}}}{{{x_2} - {x_1}}}} \right)\left( {x - {x_1}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {y - 6} \right) = - \frac{1}{3} \times \left( x \right) \\ & \Rightarrow 3y - 18 = - x \\ & \Rightarrow x + 3y = 18 \end{aligned}$$

A line passing through the origin perpendicularly cuts the line 3x - 2y = 6 at point M. Find the co-ordinates of M.
s: Equation of line perpendicular to line 3x - 2y = 6 is 2x + 3y + p = 0 As, the line passes through origin (0, 0) ∴ 2 × 0 + 3 × 0 + p = 0 ∴ p = 0 Now, the equation is 2x + 3y = 0 ∴ 2x = -3y x = $$\frac{{ - 3}}{2}$$ y By putting this value in equation 3x - 2y = 6 $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 3\left( {\frac{{ - 3}}{2}} \right)y - 2y = 6 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{ - 9}}{2}y - 2y = 6 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{ - 13y}}{2} = 6 \\ & \Rightarrow y = - \frac{{12}}{{13}} \\ & \therefore x = \frac{{ - 3}}{2} \times \left( {\frac{{ - 12}}{{13}}} \right) \\ & x = \frac{{18}}{{13}} \\ & \therefore {\text{Co - ordinate of point}} \\ & {\text{M}} = \left[ {\frac{{18}}{{13}},\, - \frac{{12}}{{13}}} \right] \end{aligned}$$

q: What would be the equation of the line, which intercepts x-axis at -5 and is perpendicular to the line y = 2x + 3?
s: Slope of line y = mx + c is m y = 2x + c, slope (m 1 ) = 2 Lines are perpendicular to each other $${m_1} = \frac{{ - 1}}{{{m_2}}}$$ Slope of perpendicular line $$\left( {{m_2}} \right) = \frac{{ - 1}}{2}$$ on x axis y = 0 Equation of line which passes through (-5, 0) (y - y 1 ) = slope (m 2 )(x - x 1 ) y - 0 = $$\frac{{ - 1}}{2}$$ (x + 5) 2y = -x - 5 x + 2y = -5

q: The length of the portion of the straight line 3x + 4y = 12 intercepted between the axes is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & 3x + 4y = 12 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{3x}}{{12}} + \frac{{4y}}{{12}} = 1 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{x}{4} + \frac{y}{3} = 1 \\ & \therefore {\text{Length of intercept AB}} = \sqrt {{4^2} + {3^3}} \\ & = \sqrt {25} \\ & = 5{\text{ units}} \end{aligned}$$

q: P(4, 2) and R(-2, 0) are vertices of a rhombus PQRS. What is the equation of diagonal QS?
s: Slope of line PR $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow {m_1} = \frac{{0 - 2}}{{ - 2 - 4}} \\ & \Rightarrow {m_1} = \frac{{ - 2}}{{ - 6}} \\ & \Rightarrow {m_1} = \frac{1}{3} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Slope of line QS = -3 = m 2 {As it is perpendicular to PR} Coordinates of point O $$\Rightarrow \left[ {\frac{{ - 2 + 4}}{2},\,\frac{{2 + 0}}{2}} \right] \Rightarrow \left( {1,\,1} \right)$$ ∴ Equation of line QS which passes through point O(1, 1) ⇒ y - 1 = m 2 (x - 1) ⇒ y - 1 = -3(x - 1) ⇒ y - 1 = -3x + 3 ⇒ 3x + y = 4

q: What is the equation of the line perpendicular to the line 2x + 3y = -6 and having Y-intercept 3?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & 2x + 3y = - 6 \\ & y = - \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{6}{3} \\ & \therefore {\text{Slope}} = - \frac{2}{3} \end{aligned}$$ ⇒ Two lines are perpendicular if m 1 × m 2 = -1 Y intercept = 3 ⇒ y = mx + c ⇒ m 2 = $$\frac{3}{2}$$ The equation of line with slope $$\frac{3}{2}$$ is:- y - y 1 = m 2 (x - x 1 ) where, (x 1 y 1 ) = (0, 3) y - 3 = $$\frac{3}{2}$$(x - 0) 2y - 6 = 3x 3x - 2y = -6

q: The line passing through the point (5, a) and point (4, 3) is perpendicular to the line x - 6y = 8. What is the value of 'a'?
s: Given, Equation of line x - 6y = 8 we write it as $$y = \frac{x}{6} - \frac{8}{6}$$ ∴ y = mx (where m is a slope) ∴ m 1 = $$\frac{1}{6}$$ If lines are perpendicular then product of their slopes is equal to -1 m 1 × m 2 = -1 ∴ $$\frac{1}{6}$$ × m 2 = -1 m 2 = - 6 ∴ Slope of perpendicular line = - 6 Perpendicular line which passes through the points (5, a) and (4, 3) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{{{y_2} - {y_1}}}{{{x_2} - {x_1}}} = {m_2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{3 - a}}{{4 - 5}} = - 6 \\ & \Rightarrow 3 - a = + 6 \times + 1 \\ & \therefore a = - 3 \end{aligned}$$

q: What is the equation of the line which intercepts x-axis and y-axis at $$\frac{3}{4}$$ and $$- \frac{2}{3}$$ respectively?
s: Equation of line which intercepts x-axis and y-axis are given below:- $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{b} = 1 \\ & {\text{where, }}a = \frac{3}{4},\,b = \frac{{ - 2}}{3}\,\,\left[ {{\text{given}}} \right] \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{x}{{\frac{3}{4}}} + \frac{y}{{\frac{{ - 2}}{3}}} = 1 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{4x}}{3} - \frac{{3y}}{2} = 1 \\ & \Rightarrow 8x - 9y = 6 \end{aligned}$$

q: The graphs of the equations 3x + y - 5 = 0 and 2x - y - 5 = 0 intersect at the point P(α, β). What is the value of (3α + β)?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & 3x + y = 5 \\ & \underline {2x - y = 5} \\ & 5x = 10 \\ & x = 2,\,y = - 1 \\ & \left( {\alpha ,\,\beta } \right) = \left( {2,\, - 1} \right) \\ & 3\alpha + \beta = 3 \times 2 - 1 = 5 \end{aligned}$$

q: The line passing through point (-3, 1) and point (x, 5) is parallel to the line passing through point (-2, -1) and point (6, 3). What is the value of x?
s: Slope (m 1 ) for the line which passes through the points (-3, 1) and (x, 5) $$= \frac{{5 - 1}}{{x + 3}} = \frac{4}{{x + 3}}$$ Similarly, slope (m 2 ) for the line which passes through the points (-2, -1) and (6, 3) $$= \frac{{3 + 1}}{{6 + 2}} = \frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}$$ If two lines are parallel to each other. $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Then, }}{m_1} = {m_2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{4}{{x + 3}} = \frac{1}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow x + 3 = 8 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 5 \end{aligned}$$

q: Slope of the line AB is $$- \frac{2}{3}.$$ Co-ordinates of points A and B are (x, -3) and (5, 2) respectively. What is the value of x?
s: Given, $$\begin{aligned} & m = \frac{{ - 2}}{3} \\ & m = \frac{{{y_2} - {y_1}}}{{{x_2} - {x_1}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{ - 2}}{3} = \frac{{2 + 3}}{{5 - x}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{ - 2}}{3} = \frac{5}{{5 - x}} \\ & \Rightarrow - 10 + 2x = 15 \\ & \Rightarrow 2x = 25 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 12.5 \end{aligned}$$

q: A(7, -8) and C(1, 4) are vertices of a square ABCD. Find equation of diagonal BD?
s: By the midpoint formula, $$\left( {\frac{{{x_1} + {x_2}}}{2},\,\frac{{{y_1} + {y_2}}}{2}} \right)$$ Midpoint of line AC $$= \left( {\frac{{7 + 1}}{2},\,\frac{{ - 8 + 4}}{2}} \right) = \left( {4,\, - 2} \right)$$ O(x 3 , y 3 ) = (4, -2) (M 1 ) Slope of line AC, $${M_1} = \frac{{{y_2} - {y_1}}}{{{x_2} - {x_1}}} = \frac{{4 - \left( { - 8} \right)}}{{1 - 7}} = - 2$$ If the lines are ⊥, then M 1 × M 2 = -1 - 2 × M 2 = -1 M 2 = $$\frac{1}{2}$$ ∴ Equation of line BD y - y 3 = M 2 (x - x 3 ) y - (-2) = $$\frac{1}{2}$$(x - 4) y + 2 = $$\frac{1}{2}$$(x - 4) x - 2y = 8
